newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Andean Pact to meet in Bogota, discuss Peru.
newsitem.headline: Andean Pact to meet in Bogota, discuss Peru.

text.p: Representatives of the Andean Pact nations will meet in Bogota on Tuesday to discuss Peru's full reincorporation into the group, Colombia's Foreign Trade Minister Carlos Ronderos said Thursday.
The recently-appointed minister said he and his counterparts would look at a fresh proposal that would permit Peru's re-entry as a full member of the pact but declined to give details.

Ronderos added that if the terms of the new deal were not accepted there would be no major impact on regional trade but said a revitalized five nation bloc would strengthen its bargaining position in negotiations for a free trade zone with the Southern Cone Common Market MERCOSUR.

Peru partially withdrew from the pact in 1992 amid differences over its trade tariffs policy. member nations failed to agree Peru's full reinstatement at a recent meeting in Lima saying pledges to harmonize tariffs by the year 2005 were insufficient.

At Thursday's press conference, Ronderos played down recent criticisms that the Andean Pact had lost credibility, saying: "The situation has been tremendously distorted. What's happening is that this is generating panic and that could be harmful to Colombia and its investors. The Andean Pact is far from dead."
The Andean Pact was formed 1969 in an effort to boost levels of integration and cooperation between member states and strengthen solidarity ties in the sub-region.
